newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz sees EMU costs at 100 mln dmk.
newsitem.headline: Allianz sees EMU costs at 100 mln dmk.

text.p: German insurance group Allianz AG Holding on Friday predicted the conversion to a single European currency would cost it some 100 million marks.

According to a summary of comments by chief financial officer Diethart Breipohl at a seminar in Karlsruhe, Allianz does not expect the Euro, so long as it is stable, to trigger additional investment risks.
Breipohl said there was therefore no reason to change current investment strategies by switching to short term deposits or into francs or dollars.
Breipohl also said the currency union, scheduled to begin in January 1999, should bring major opportunities for capital investment, allowing access to a larger and more varied stock and bond market.

For Allianz, achieving a more international capital investment package would be one of the most important goals for the next few years, he said. Already the group was 36 percent invested abroad, counting its subsidiaries.
European demographics and the exhaustion of social security systems in the region would create above-average growth opportunities for life and health insurers, he said.
Breipohl also predicted that the arrival of the Euro would accelerate the concentration process in the financial services sector in general.
